payload.root_cause: In pyshop/pricing.py, `promo_pct` evaluates the promo validity window with an inclusive upper bound: `if promo["start"] <= today <= promo["end"]:` (line 45). The domain rule (stated in the function's own docstring at line 39 and in README.md) is that `start` is inclusive but `end` is EXCLUSIVE. Because the comparison uses `<=` on the end date, when `today == promo["end"]` (e.g., SPRING10 on 2026-06-01, whose end is date(2026,6,1) per line 11) the code returns promo["pct"] (10) instead of 0. The correct condition is `promo["start"] <= today < promo["end"]`. The PROMOS data itself is correct; only the boundary check is wrong.

payload.rationale: The root cause is the inclusive upper bound in the promo validity check. In `promo_pct` (pyshop/pricing.py:45), the condition `promo["start"] <= today <= promo["end"]` returns the promo percentage when `today == promo["end"]`, but both the function's docstring (line 39) and README.md specify that `end` is exclusive. Changing the second `<=` to `<` makes the window [start, end), so SPRING10 (end = 2026-06-01) is no longer accepted on June 1st, 2026, while still returning 10 on 2026-03-01 and 2026-05-31 and 0 before the start date — matching tests/test_pricing.py:24-28. No other code or data changes are needed since the PROMOS dates and all other logic are correct.
